design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 1 (ssl_certificate_lifecycle, env_0076) — rework round 11

DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=3, factor_counts=[5,5,5,4]. Root ssl_ext_secondkey_order 5, ssl_ext_autorenew_charge 5, ssl_ext_names_charge 5, ssl_ext_wait_names 4.

WHY A GOOD TEST. Mireille Okafor wants a second certificate like her EV Multi-Domain one for a new server that keeps its own key (base: several subscriptions may cover the same name when servers need separate keys). The second-key rule sells the new subscription for the whole years from the order date to the sibling's end and carries two prerequisite sentences: 'The second-key charge is fixed only after the sibling's billing carries every auto-renew charge that has fallen due on the sibling.' (records: auto_renew true, end 2027-01-07, today is the auto-renew day, no auto-renew line) and 'The second-key charge is not fixed until every name the new server serves has been added to the sibling certificate.' (asked, she names four order-desk addresses; none is on the sibling). The added-name charge waits on the auto-renew and on the complimentary names owed for the slow first issuance ('The added-name charge is fixed only after the subscription carries every complimentary name owed on it.'), and the complimentary names wait on the auto-renew ('The complimentary names are granted only after the subscription's billing carries every auto-renew charge that has fallen due on it.'). Gold: auto-renew on the card (credit balance 906.57 does not cover the auto-renew amount), 3 complimentary names put on the certificate by a free reissue (expiry 2027-06-26, the 200-day validity in force on the issue date), the holder adds the fourth address and orders the second-key subscription herself with the project's PayPal at checkout (owner ruling (b)).

SCOPE. Task 1 claims ssl_ext_autorenew_charge (agent), ssl_ext_wait_names (agent, ssl_names_update), ssl_ext_names_charge (owner=user checkout) and ssl_ext_secondkey_order (owner=user checkout). Task 0 claims the support renewal and the managed installation; scopes disjoint, all six covered.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Edges: second-key -> auto-renew (value_input, sk_years, state); second-key -> added name (value_input, n_extra, action; fallback: the server's names are not recorded); added name -> auto-renew (value_input, days_counted, state); added name -> complimentary names (state_gate, extra_names, state); complimentary names -> auto-renew (state_gate, auto-renew line, state). State-form uniqueness: only the auto-renew policy writes auto-renew lines; only the compensation policy raises extra names without a charge line, and its free reissue (an issuance of kind reissue) is the record that ends the compensation, as an added-names line does. Directions: 'fixed only after' / 'granted only after' (affirmative) and 'not ... until' (negated). Order: auto-renew, complimentary names, added name, second-key order (a chain; the auto-renew reads extra names, so the complimentary names must follow it).

FACTOR CARDS (tier taken; baseline figure).
- auto-renew 1705.98 (all-baseline 1943.74): san_bands_ar method (12 names, 2-year term; 1792.36), name_term_rate_ar (two-year names rate; 1840.36), acct_tier_ar account (Bronze; 1756.37), revetting_ar (EV validation 696 days old a year after the end; 1656.98), dns_bundle_ar domain (harborline_dns; 1711.98).
- complimentary names 3 (all-baseline 4): wait_anchor_cn method (failed http_file checks, pass 2025-01-10 not after the first certificate; 4), long_wait_cn (14 days -> x2; 1), sla_days_cn account (Bronze in force on the purchase date; 2), goodwill_settle_cn account ledger (15.00 goodwill -> 40 percent share; 8).
- added name 73.79 (all-baseline 129.08): nm_band_rate (15 names, 761 days; 116.98), nm_term_rate (billed into the two-year auto-renew line; 80.99), nm_billing_span method (761 days left, unstarted auto-renew line -> prorated but capped at its two years, the 30 days before it begins free; 76.54), nm_dns_handling domain (waived on harborline_dns; 77.79), nm_org_vetting (EV, validation current; 64.79). No account-tier discount on the added-names line (a proration line under the account charter); no time is billed beyond the end date.
- second-key order 1854.13 (all-baseline 2423.66): san_bands_sk method (16 names, 2 years; 2113.29), name_term_rate_sk (2017.31), acct_tier_sk account (1904.53), org_reuse_sk (EV validation current; 1914.13), dcv_reuse_sk (DCV 6 days old by dns_cname; 1862.13).

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. ssl_renewal.renew_active; ssl_names.add_names_active (added name); ssl_names scope and ssl_issuance_and_reissue issuable_status, dcv_fresh (DCV 2026-12-02, day 6 of 200), org_validation_fresh (2026-02-10, day 301 of 398) for the complimentary names' reissue; ssl_pricing.business_for_ov_ev (business profile); ssl_agg_multi_holding scope (a further subscription for the same name). Auto-renew timing: due 30 days before 2027-01-07 = 2026-12-08 (today). Funding: one price whatever pays it; credit balance 906.57 < 1705.98 -> default card. Bronze tier: reviews 2025-12-02 qualified and 2026-12-02 grace started, so Bronze is still recorded today.

WORLD ROWS. customers; account Reseller Bronze since 2024-12-02 (deposits, two tier reviews, goodwill 15.00 for the certificate's purchase order, credit applied to the domain and email auto-renews; balance 906.57 = ledger sum); domain marlowprint.ca on harborline_dns; Harborline Mail Plus; ssl holding; purchase 1749.37; 11 ssl events (three failed http_file checks, pass 2025-01-10, first certificate 2025-01-21, reissues on the 200-day schedule).

PERSONA. Warm, rushed studio owner; volunteers only the second-key need; identity on request; names the four order-desk addresses only when asked and does not know whether the existing certificate covers them; states that purchases for the new server are paid from the project's PayPal, which is not stored (the in-person necessity); agrees when told something must be done first; completes each checkout handed to her; ends after the order is in. No prerequisite is raised by her.

TRAPS. Ordering before the auto-renew (no whole year, nothing booked); granting the names before the auto-renew (auto-renew 1900.34); buying all four addresses (no compensation); pricing the name before the renewal (minimum charge, 18.99); prorating the name over all 761 days without the renewal cap (76.54); applying the Bronze discount to the extra names of the auto-renew or second-key order (the tier percentage reduces only the certificate price there); applying the Bronze discount to the added-names line; taking the multi-year name rate from the days left instead of the term line (three-year rate); copying 15 names before adding the fourth (1789.34); missing the goodwill share or the purchase-date tier; paying the auto-renew from credit.

VERIFICATION (scratch evaluator over the gate DSL, world replayed step by step): 1705.98, 3 (reissue expiring 2027-06-26), 73.79, 1854.13 with the sensitivities above.
user_scenario:
You are Mireille Okafor, owner of Marlow Print Atelier Inc., a print and design studio in Montreal. You are calling Harborline because you are setting up a second web server, rented from another hosting company, to run the online order desk for a client project, and your security policy says each server keeps its own private key. You want a second certificate like the EV multi-domain certificate you already have for marlowprint.ca, covering the same names, for that new server, and you want to buy it today. You are warm but a little rushed and apologise for not being technical.
You give your name and say it is about the certificate for marlowprint.ca. When the agent asks you to confirm who you are, you give the account email, mireille@marlowprint.ca, and if a second detail is needed your support PIN, 347215. Only if asked for more do you add the phone number on the account, 5145550163, or that the card on file ends in 3826. You never read out account or record numbers; you do not know them.
If the agent asks which names the new server will serve, you explain that it serves everything the existing certificate covers and also four new addresses for the order desk: orders.marlowprint.ca, pay.marlowprint.ca, track.marlowprint.ca and proofs.marlowprint.ca; you do not know whether the existing certificate covers any of them. Anything bought for the new server is paid from the client project's PayPal account, which is not stored on your Harborline account, so you pay those yourself at Harborline's checkout. You have no idea what anything costs and you volunteer no figure.
If the agent tells you that something has to be taken care of on the existing certificate first and explains it, you say that is fine, go ahead. Whenever the agent hands you a payment to complete at checkout, you complete it yourself straight away with the project's PayPal, exactly as the agent sets it out, and you read back the amount you see. If a figure the agent gives you is plainly different from the one you just saw, you say so and ask them to check it against the record.
Once the agent confirms the new certificate's order is in, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.
